title: Lecithin, 21 CFR 184.1400, and enzyme-modified lecithin, 21 CFR 184.1063: direct food substances affirmed as generally recognized as safe
journal: Code of Federal Regulations, title 21, sections 184.1400 and 184.1063, read in the electronic Code of Federal Regulations, title 21 amended to 14 October 2026
funder: US Food and Drug Administration; the text is federal regulation codified by the Office of the Federal Register.
result: Section 184.1400: commercial lecithin is a naturally occurring mixture of the phosphatides of choline, ethanolamine and inositol, with smaller amounts of other lipids, isolated as a gum following hydration of solvent-extracted soy, safflower or corn oils, bleached if desired by hydrogen peroxide and benzoyl peroxide and dried by heating; it meets the specifications of the Food Chemicals Codex, 3rd edition (1981), pages 166 to 167; in accordance with 184.1(b)(1) the ingredient is used in food with no limitation other than current good manufacturing practice; prior sanctions different from the uses established in the section do not exist or have been waived. Source: 48 FR 51150, 7 November 1983. Section 184.1063: enzyme-modified lecithin is prepared by treating lecithin with phospholipase A2 (EC 3.1.1.4) or pancreatin; specifications include acetone-insoluble matter (phosphatides) not less than 50.0%, acid value not more than 40, lead not more than 1.0 part per million, hexane-insoluble matter not more than 0.3%, peroxide value not more than 20, water not more than 4.0% and lysolecithin 50 to 80 mole percent of total phosphatides; in accordance with 184.1(b)(1) the ingredient is used in food with no limitation other than current good manufacturing practice, the affirmation resting on use as an emulsifier as defined in 170.3(o)(8) at levels not exceeding current good manufacturing practice. Source: 61 FR 45889, 30 August 1996, as amended at 78 FR 14666, 81 FR 5595 and 88 FR 17724. Neither section sets a numerical limit on intake or use.
